articles.title: The Rise of the Billionaire Lobby
articles.author: Ben Case
articles.content_excerpt: You’ve heard of the oil lobby, the tobacco lobby, the Israel lobby, the charter school lobby. Behind all of these are billionaires who benefit from the underlying industries or sectors, and whose corporations use their resources to lobby the government for favorable policies. Now, in reaction to a California ballot initiative for the world’s first billionaire tax, we have an innovation: a lobby for billionaires themselves. Self-advocacy by wealthy people is nothing new, of course. articles.title: Decades of Growing Inequality Powered MAGA’s Rise
articles.author: Thomas Ferguson
articles.content_excerpt: What lies behind the ascendance of Donald Trump and his Make America Great Again movement? All sorts of demagogic political appeals — racism, sexism, anti-immigrant stereotyping — have played integral roles in the rise of the Right, of course. But a fundamental underlying driver is popular disillusionment with an economy that has for decades failed millions of people.That is the argument of our new working paper for the Institute for New Economic Thinking (INET), which analyzes the macroeconomic roots of the collapse of the political center in the United States. articles.title: We Must Talk about Denuclearizing Israel
articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: There is a simple action DSA can take to dramatically change the relationship between the United States and the genocidal regime in Israel. Start talking about their nukes. Openly, aggressively. Denounce Israel as a rogue nuclear state. Since Israel began developing its nuclear program in the 1950s, its nuclear capabilities have remained the subject of longstanding secrecy and diplomatic silence. The U.S. government has refused to acknowledge Israeli weapons for a variety of reasons; a big one is that a Presidential determination would trigger the stiff sanctions in Sec. 102(B) of the Arms Export Control Act. articles.title: The Sewer Socialists Were Pragmatic Class Warriors
articles.author: Eric Blanc
articles.content_excerpt: Milwaukee, Wisconsin, was a Socialist Party stronghold for much of the first half of the twentieth century. Socialists there built a strong presence in the labor movement and city council and held the mayor’s office for nearly forty years between 1910 and 1960. The Milwaukee socialists’ focus on good governance and municipal policy achievements like clean water earned them the ire of some fellow socialists, who derisively dubbed them “sewer socialists.” Yet New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has cited them as an inspiration for his own administration, and, as Jacobin contributor Eric Blanc argued in an essay for Catalyst earlier this year, the sewer socialists’ pragmatic approach to building working-class power has much to teach the Left today. articles.title: In Defense of Victor Serge
articles.author: Claudio Albertani
articles.content_excerpt: For decades, anyone writing about Victor Serge had to begin by explaining who he was and why we should care. Despite an enormous literary legacy, he had been literally airbrushed from Soviet history, a forgotten figure even on much of the Left. History is rarely kind to the vanquished, and Serge stood on the side of the defeated, with those who refused to compromise with capitalism or surrender to Stalinism. The cost was high, but Serge’s eloquent voice and mighty pen could not prevent his being sidelined by history, ignored or poorly understood, consigned to a life of poverty. Four of his books were confiscated by the Soviet Censorship ( Glavlit ), and other writings were left unpublished, though they establish him as a man who belongs to our future. Who was Serge? articles.title: Coalitions Make the Left Stronger
articles.author: Midwestern Socialist -- Chicago DSA
articles.content_excerpt: DSA has had a string of spectacular electoral victories. With success comes greater media attention, growing membership, and new challenges. One of the most important questions is how to build broad unity that can achieve transformative policies. And how do we criticize each other and political allies without falling into sectarian purism where differences overshadow what we hold in common and disrupt working together? The specter haunting DSA seems to be the possibility of socialist congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (AOC) joining the presidential primary. Positions within the organization range from enthusiastic support, to begrudging inevitability, to outright opposition. But the debate over AOC is just the tip of the iceberg. articles.title: Under Israeli Settler Attacks, I Feel I Am Not Alive
articles.author: Miriame Mazid
articles.content_excerpt: In the West Bank village of At-Tuwani this July 19, Ruqayya Rabe’i, three months pregnant, lay in her room beside her four sleeping daughters. At 12:30 a.m., the first stones hit her home. She rushed to check the front door. There in the living room, she found her fifteen-year-old son, Usayd, sleeping directly below a window where, according to Ruqayya, several settlers were armed with guns and knives and trying to force their way in. She tried to shake her son awake, but he didn’t stir. When the settlers noticed her, she fled, certain that if they saw him, they would shoot. The window was shattered, a chemical compound poured through it, and the frame went up in flames, Ruqayya said.
